slides.title: 1. Drawing Markers with Point Dropper
slides.html:
• Point Dropper is the tool to draw Markers to the map.
  • Markers you draw are not automatically sent anywhere. Check Sending a Marker for guide how to send them.
  • Tap the Point Dropper when you want to draw markers to the map.

slides.title: 2. Specify Marker Type
slides.html:
• Tap "Ground" to specify your marker's subtype further if you so wish.
  • You can edit the marker's types later too.

slides.title: 3. Select Marker Affiliation
slides.html: • Tap Unknown, Neutral, Enemy and Friendly for affiliation and to start dropping your new Marker.

slides.title: 4. Tap on map to drop the pointer
slides.html:
• The pointer spawns upon tap.
  • It is present only in your local device now - see Sending a Marker guide on sharing options.

slides.title: 5. Select Marker for Editing or Send
slides.html:
• Tap the marker to bring up the action menu.
  • Tap the details icon. It is right next of the delete icon to fill details.

slides.title: 6. Open the Name dialog
slides.html: • Tap on the generated name of your marker, in order to edit it.

slides.title: 7. Name your Marker
slides.html:
• Name your marker according to your unit's convention.
  • This example follows the following scheme: "Reporting unit name, Descriptive Title."

slides.title: 8. Change Type
slides.html: • Tap Type to edit the marker subtype, similarily as before.

slides.title: 9. Type Choices
slides.html: • There is plenty of choice for marker subtypes. Specify yours, if applicable.

slides.title: 10. Set Location Error (Optional)
slides.html:
• You can specify the location error of your symbol if applicable.
  • It describes how accurate your marker's geolocation is. This is important in case the marker could be a target for fires.

slides.title: 11. Location Error Choices
slides.html:
• As of NATO standard, you may specify the error from CAT1 (lowest) to CAT6 (highest error).
  • CAT1: 0-6m. CAT2: 7-15m. CAT3: 16-30m. CAT4: 31-91m. CAT5: 92-305m. CAT6: 305+m.

slides.title: 12. Specify Marker Size (Optional)
slides.html:
• If your marker subtype is "Unit", you can specify the markers' size indication (eg. squad, platoon, company).
  • Tap Unit Modifier/Echelon to do that.

slides.title: 13. Specify Marker Size (Optional)
slides.html: • Choose the marker's size as applicable.

slides.title: 14. Fill in details using Remarks
slides.html: • Write details about the marker by scrolling down and tapping the pen icon.

slides.title: 15. Fill in the details
slides.html: • Fill in details as needed.

slides.title: 16. Edit marker's Status
slides.html:
• If applicable, you can alter the Status of this marker.
  • This is usable if you edit an existing marker to reflect a change, or are planning an anticipated action.

slides.title: 17. Edit spotting Sensors
slides.html: • If you happen to have sensor, eg. video stream, going on against the target, you can fill that by tapping the "play" icon.

slides.title: 18. Add a video sensor to a marker
slides.html:
• Connect a stream to this marker, either a stream from Deploy App's MediaMTX [separate guide] or from a platform like YouTube.
  • You have to specify address, port, protocol and possibly a password for let the stream to be shown in ATAK.
  • This will be instructed in the Deploy App MediaMTX guide.

slides.title: 19. Adding attachments
slides.html:
• You can attachments, eg. images, to your marker.
  • To do so, tap the pin icon.

slides.title: 20. Adding an attachment
slides.html: • You can eg. shoot a fresh image, or choose from your images using Image File.

slides.title: 21. Adding an image
slides.html: • When you are done adding attachments, go back to the main marker details screen via the back arrow.

slides.title: 22. Remember: There's no automatic send
slides.html:
• Any marker you draw exists on your device only, unless you send the marker to somebody.
  • See the next guide page for marker sending options.
